‘step’-function family

1 Overview

This document provides an overview of improveR’s functions focused on working with steps.

Steps are the fundamental building blocks of every analytical workflow within the improve framework. Each step contains

  • at least one R script containing the relevant code
  • linked or embedded resources (e.g., input files) and any output files (e.g., reports, graphs) stored in the step’s inventory
  • tools and their definitions to orchestrate the script’s execution and file creation

Groupped by their role in the overall analysis, they constitute an analysis tree (e.g. analysis tree ‘Exploratory Data Analysis’).

Critically, by linking one step’s output as an input to another step, steps can be ‘horizontally’ chained together to an integrated workflow. This workflow can span across the entire or only parts of the analytical pipeline from the initial import of raw data (e.g. originating from a dataorder specification), via the exploratory data analysis, statistical modeling, to the reporting and eventual review. This integration of steps is instrumental when it comes to streamlining the entire workflow and ensuring reproducibility of the final results.

Equally important is improve’s ability to organize steps in a vertical hierarchy by introducing parent-child relations between them. A child step can be a modified copy of a parent step, e.g. created to inquire into the consequences of a specific modification within the step’s code. Similarly, a step can be attached to a parent step due to substantive considerations of the analyst, reflecting a thematic or conceptual hierarchy between them.

The above outlined two perspectives are central when it comes to the understanding of the concepts of lineage and usage on one hand, and child and parenton the other hand. These terms are ubiquitous when working with the improve in general and step-related functions in particular.

The hierarchical parent-child relationship is conceptually different to the horizontal relationship between two steps within a workflow. Step A can produce results which are ‘used’ by Step B. But this does not make Step A a parent of Step B. Similarly, Step B is not a child of Step A even if if Step A is within the lineage of Step B. Keeping this conceptual distinction in mind is critical.

  • Workflow, or input/output-centered perspective: Looks horizontally at how a chain of steps (in analysis trees) transforms an input into some output. This view is visualized in improve’s Data Manipulation Graph (as shown above).

  • File-centric perspective: Focuses on how files inside different steps are related in terms of their creation, which is more akin to a vertical angle. This perspective is visualized in improve client’s editor view when displaying an analysis tree (as above in Figure 1).

With this as the background, the current document goes beyond the primarily technical focus of the function references/help files, and seeks to demonstrate the actual application of the step-function family. To do so, throughout the document references to various examples are included.

2 getStep

2.1 Purpose of the function

getStep is pivotal when it comes to working with steps. Calling the function on a step returns a detailed environment object which not only encompasses information on the the step’s own properties, but also on its relation with other steps within the wider workflow as well as additional function definitions to work with this information.

2.2 Relation to other functions [review/shorten]

Within the step functions family, getStep functions as the central orchestrator. It bridges lower-level step construction functions with higher-level workflow operations. The function builds directly upon createStepEnv as its foundational building block. It complements step modification functions like attachStep, detachStep, changeStepDescription, and changeStepRationale by providing the rich environment context needed for these operations.

The function creates a bidirectional relationship with navigation functions such as loadChildSteps, loadParentStep, and loadChildResources. This relationship uses sophisticated lazy-loading mechanisms that populate relationship data only when accessed. This approach optimizes performance while maintaining full navigational capabilities.

In the broader improveR ecosystem, getStep serves as a critical integration point. It connects individual step management with workflow-level orchestration through getWorkflow. The function supports execution coordination with functions like finishRunResource and runStepResource. It interfaces with the distributed resource management system through authenticated REST API calls and intelligent caching strategies. The environments generated by getStep provide the foundational data structures and operational interfaces that enable complex workflow operations, dependency tracking, and coordinated multi-step analytical pipeline execution.

2.3 Under the hood [review]

The implementation architecture follows a three-phase orchestration pattern. This pattern ensures robust step environment creation while maintaining optimal performance and data consistency.

The initial phase involves calling getStepDf to retrieve comprehensive step metadata from the server. It performs validation to ensure the step identifier exists and is accessible. The phase extracts critical information including process configurations, file relationships, and execution history.

The second phase establishes workflow context through createWorkflow. This initializes the shared environment that enables cross-step dependency tracking, workflow-level method binding, and coordinated execution planning capabilities.

The final construction phase calls createStepEnv with the validated step dataframe and initialized workflow context. It systematically builds the multi-layered environment structure. This structure includes nested sub-environments for relationships (children, parent, usage, lineage), functional bindings for operations like getStepInventory() and getStepState(), lazy-loading mechanisms for performance optimization, and self-referential structures that enable method chaining and intuitive navigation.

This orchestrated approach ensures that the resulting environment object provides a comprehensive, consistent, and performant interface for all step-related operations. It maintains proper integration with the broader improveR workflow ecosystem.

2.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Start

To demonstrate the application of getStep() see the example below. As an input the function takes a step’s ident, which can be its path, resource (version) id, full entity (version) id, or short entitiy (version) id.

Example getStep(): Apply function
identATModelingStep1 <- "/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1" 
envATModelingStep1 <- getStep(identATModelingStep1)
class(envATModelingStep1)
## [1] "environment"

The returned result is an environment with multiple bindings of different classes.

Example getStep(): Overview of obtained elements’ class
tibble(
  name = ls(envATModelingStep1),
  class = purrr::map_chr(name, \(x) class(get(x, envir = envATModelingStep1)))
) %>% arrange(class)
## # A tibble: 13 × 2
##    name                class      
##    <chr>               <chr>      
##  1 stepDf              data.frame 
##  2 children            environment
##  3 lineage             environment
##  4 parent              environment
##  5 this                environment
##  6 usage               environment
##  7 workflow            environment
##  8 createTemplate      function   
##  9 getStepInventory    function   
## 10 getStepResource     function   
## 11 getStepState        function   
## 12 getStepWithoutCache function   
## 13 retrieveMainProcess function

The viewer below allows for a closer look at each of the elements.

getStepInventory, getStepState, getStepWithoutCache, getStepResource, retrieveMainProcess and createTemplate contain all function defintions, meaning these functions can be called on the obtained environment to get additional details or trigger other actions.

2.5 Details

For a thorough understanding of the output of getStep(), the sections below will look into each element of the obtained step environment.

But before diving into the details some conceptual clarification on the differences between child and parent on the one hand, and usage and lineage on the other hand.

The parent-child relationship is characterized by its vertical hierarchy. This hierarchy can originate from the child’s origin (a copy of the parent child) or due to a substantive connection between two steps, which

children

Show details

The environment of our loaded step improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1 contains the element children which is again of class environment. Checking its content reveals that at this point it contains a single element: the function load(). Once this function is called, children becomes additionally populated by four steps.

Call load() function in ‘children’
ls(envATModelingStep1$children)
## [1] "load"

#call function load()
envATModelingStep1$children$load()
## 2025-10-07 18:18:44.841953 INFO::adding  Step 7 ST-54672 to children
## 2025-10-07 18:18:47.14868 INFO::adding  Step 6 ST-54651 to children
## 2025-10-07 18:18:49.407719 INFO::adding  Step 8 ST-54675 to children
## 2025-10-07 18:18:51.613646 INFO::adding  Step 1 ST-65316 to children
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$children))

This result is consistent with the result returned by improveR’s getChildSteps() or the pertaining graph in the improve client.

Get Step 1’s children
childATModelingStep1 <- improveR::loadChildSteps("/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1")$data[[1]]
nrow(childATModelingStep1)
## [1] 4
childATModelingStep1 %>% select(path, description)
##                                path                  description
## 1 /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 7   Model: Duration ~ Wt + Age
## 2 /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 6 Model 2: Duration ~ Wt + Sex
## 3 /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 8 Model: Duration ~ Wt+Age+Sex
## 4   /improve-tutorial/Review/Step 1       Model 1: Duration ~ Wt

Once loaded, navigating from i.e. Step 1 to its children can be conveniently done by simply adding the step’s location to the call, e.g. envATModelingStep1$children$'Modeling/Step 7/54672'.

Note that navigating from one step to the next using the $ operator is facilitated by autocompletion when used in the terminal of RStudio or Positron IDEs (or VS Code with radian extension).

In terms of its structure, the obtained environment of the child step is identical to the one previously obtained for Step 1 and contains again 13 elements, including children and parent.

Below the elements of Modeling/Step 7/54672’s environment.

Structure and Content of child environment
class(envATModelingStep1$children$`Modeling/Step 7/54672`)
## [1] "environment"
listviewer::jsonedit(list(envATModelingStep1$children$`Modeling/Step 7/54672`))

parent

Show details

Let’s now focus on the element parent in the environment of Step 1, as initially retrieved via getStep().

As with the above described element children, the nested environment parent initially also contains only the function load().

Calling the function here, on /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1, does not return a step since Step 1 does not have a parent (see the image of the analysis tree ‘Modeling’ above, Figure 1). Consequently, the function load() remains the only element of the environment parent.

Trying to load parent of Step 1 which has no parent
#content of 'parent'
ls(envATModelingStep1$parent)
## [1] "load"

#trigger function 'load()'
envATModelingStep1$parent$load()

#content of 'parent' is unchanged
ls(envATModelingStep1$parent)
## [1] "load"
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$parent))

To properly demonstrate the use of the parent element, let us get a different step, i.e. /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 8 which has Step 1 as a parent (see again above, Figure 1).

Load parent of Step 8
#get Step 8
envATModelingStep8 <- getStep("/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 8") 

#function load() is initially the only element of the parent environment
ls(envATModelingStep8$parent)
## [1] "load"

#call function load()
envATModelingStep8$parent$load()

#`parent` is is now featuring a new element, Step 1
ls(envATModelingStep8$parent)
## [1] "load"                  "Modeling/Step 1/54635"
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep8$parent))

As shown above, after calling the load() function on the parent environment of Step 8, a new element is added: Modeling/Step 1/54635, which - as we know from above - is the parent of Step 8.

usage

Show details

The element usage in Step 1’s environment refers to those steps which are directly (‘consumers’) or indirectly (‘indirect consumers’) depending on this step within a specific workflow. ‘Depending’ means in this context that the results produced by the step are used by the subsequent steps. The covered steps are ‘to the right’ or ‘downstream’ in the analysis.

Let’s demonstrate this with the specific example of Step /improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1.

After having obtained a step’s environment, its usage related data is not yet available. Solely the function load() is available in envATModelingStep1$usage. Only after having called the function, envATModelingStep1$usage contains details on the downstream steps.

Load usage of Step 1
ls(envATModelingStep1$usage) #function `load()` sole element of `usage`
## [1] "load"

envATModelingStep1$usage$load(stepDepth=-1, treeDepth=-1) #call `load()`
## 2025-10-07 18:19:00.042807 INFO::adding  Step 1 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-62516 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:03.68123 INFO::adding  Step 10 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-59463 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:05.553587 INFO::adding  Step 9 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-54678 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:10.47796 INFO::adding  Step 1 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-64312 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:12.396837 WARNING::Resource with ID: envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:FI-54665 could not be loaded
## 2025-10-07 18:19:13.5782 WARNING::Resource with ID: envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:FI-56117 could not be loaded
## 2025-10-07 18:19:14.051772 WARNING::Resource with ID: envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:FI-54665 could not be loaded
## 2025-10-07 18:19:14.140945 WARNING::Resource with ID: envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:FI-56117 could not be loaded

ls(envATModelingStep1$usage) 
## [1] "load"                   "Modeling/Step 10/59463" "Modeling/Step 9/54678"  "Reporting/Step 1/62516" "Reporting/Step 1/64312"
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1))

The usage element provides insights into all steps that directly or indirectly depend on the current step within a workflow. After calling load(), the environment is populated with downstream step information, allowing the user to trace how the step’s results propagate through the analysis.

How encompassing a step’s usage is loaded, i.e. how far downstream steps should retrieved, is specified by the load() function’s stepDepth and treeDepth parameters. A value of stepDepth==1 covers all steps which are directly following the step in question. A value of 2 casts the net wider and returns also those steps which are directly following the steps which were retrieved with the value 1. The value can be increased as deemed useful. A value of -1 is the most far-reaching and returns all steps which make use of the initially retrieved step.

Similarly, the function argument treeDepth defines over how many analysis trees a step’s usage should be loaded.

Parameter stepDepth and treeDepth
envATModelingStep1 <- getStep("/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1")
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1))
Parameter stepDepth and treeDepth

envATModelingStep1$usage$load(stepDepth=1, treeDepth=1)
## 2025-10-07 18:19:35.560467 INFO::adding  Step 1 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-62516 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:36.59023 INFO::adding  Step 10 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-59463 to usage
## 2025-10-07 18:19:37.614577 INFO::adding  Step 9 envhost1.hc.scintecodev.internal-5310:ST-54678 to usage
envATModelingStep1$usage$load(treeDepth=0)

listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$usage))

Note: The Data Manipulation Graph (DMG) in the improve client currently does not show consumer steps outside a step’s own analysis tree.

lineage

Show details

The element lineage inside Step 1’s environment is the counterpart to usage. It includes steps which are upstream or ‘to the left’ of Step 1. In other words, it refers to those steps of which the step in question, i.e. here Step 1 of the analysis tree ‘Modeling’, is depending on. The parameter stepDepth and treeDepth again define the scope (or width) of the function call load().

Get lineage - PENDING/CURRENTLY NOT WORKING
envATModelingStep1 <- getStep("/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1")
ls(envATModelingStep1$lineage) #shows only fn load, OK
## [1] "load"
Code
envATModelingStep1$lineage$load(stepDepth=-1, treeDepth=-1)
x <- envATModelingStep1$workflow$df()

envATModelingStep1$lineage$load(treeDepth=-1)
ls(envATModelingStep1$lineage) 
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$lineage))

ls(envATModelingStep1$lineage$`EDA/Step 5/54047`$workflow$df)

Note that the DMG viewer of the improve client displays the entire lineage, including also preceding analysis trees.

stepDf

Show details

stepDf is another element included in the environment which was returned by getStep(). It is a data frame and contains metadata on step 1. Two columns in stepDf should be highlight here: processes and remote Files.

processes is a list column (a nested data frame) which provides details on the tool and related processes steering the execution of step 1. This data reflects the information shown in the tool tab of the step in improve’s client.

Details of stepDf
class(envATModelingStep1$stepDf)
## [1] "data.frame"
names(envATModelingStep1$stepDf)
##  [1] "handle"         "processes"      "treeIdent"      "treeName"       "treePath"       "description"    "rationale"      "sourceEntityId" "sourceName"     "remoteFiles"    "fullName"
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$stepDf))
Details of stepDf

envATModelingStep1$stepDf$processes[[1]]
##                                 handle runserverLabel toolLabel toolInstance                                                                                                                                                                    toolArgs   toolStreamablePatterns selected gridTool main name processType position gridArguments

The second column of stepDf which needs highlighting is remoteFiles. It is again a list-column containing a data frame. This data frame presents details on those files which are inputs into step 1, and get further processed when the step is executed. Critically, it also features the column asLink which indicates whether the file is stored inside the step’s inventory or linked from another step.

Code
class(envATModelingStep1$stepDf$remoteFiles)
## [1] "list"

envATModelingStep1$stepDf$remoteFiles[[1]][c("name", "variableName", "ident", "asLink", "variableProcess")]

getStepInventory

Show details

The binding getStepInventory stored inside Step 1’s environment is of class function and contains the function definition.

Definition of getStepInventory
class(envATModelingStep1$getStepInventory)
## [1] "function"

Calling the function returns the inventory of Step 1. Note that in contrast to the above described load() functions related to children and parent, the getStepInventory() function does not load the inventory into the step’s environment, but returns it as a data frame. In other words, while envATModelingStep1$children$load() triggers a ‘side-effect’ to modify the step’s environment, getStepInventory() does not modify the environment but returns its output. The returned data frame contains the list column data which provides the details on each of the inventory’s files.

Apply function
#apply function to Step 1's environment
stepInventory <- envATModelingStep1$getStepInventory()

stepInventoryData <- stepInventory %>%
unnest_longer(data) %>%
unnest_wider(data, names_sep="_")

class(stepInventory)

2.6 workflow

envStep$workflow is only populated after having called lineage(). It subsequently contains several elements which are described below.

Details of workflow

  name = ls(envATModelingStep1$workflow),

) %>% arrange(class)

rerunAll

The rerunAll() function re-executes all steps in the workflow from scratch in the correct dependency order. It completely re-executes the entire workflow, running every step regardless of whether files have changed or are outdated.

Internally, it creates a full execution plan by calling createReexecutionPlan(), executes the plan by calling executePlan(), and invisibly returns the newly executed workflow.

The rerunAll() function is essentially a convenience wrapper that combines creating a full execution plan with immediately executing it, providing a simple way to completely refresh a workflow’s execution state.

Call rerunAll()
envATModelingStep1$workflow$rerunAll()

Comparison with other workflow functions:

  • rerunChangedAndOutdated(): Only reruns steps with changed/outdated files and their consumers
  • createFullExecutionPlan(): Creates the same plan but doesn’t execute it
  • executePlan(plan): Executes a specific custom plan

internalLinks (env)

The environment binding internalLinks contains a data frame which serves as the workflow’s ‘dependency graph’. It tracks file relationships between steps with columns like sourceStep, targetStep , entityId, path, and metadata for change detection. It is populated by analyzing each step’s remoteFiles to identify internal dependencies versus external files.

This structure enables intelligent workflow execution by determining proper step ordering, identifying which steps need re-execution when files change, and automatically including downstream dependencies. Functions like createReexecutionPlan() use this data to build execution plans that only run necessary steps while maintaining data consistency.

The dependency graph transforms complex file relationships into a queryable structure that answers questions like “what depends on Step A?” and “if this file changes, what needs re-running?” This enables efficient incremental execution and automated change propagation throughout the workflow.

Show internalLinks
envATModelingStep1$workflow$internalLinks
## NULL

files (env)

Empty.

outputFiles (env)

Empty.

steps (env)

The element steps in the workflow environment contains all steps which form part of the workflow. Here, steps contains five elements.

It contains the meta data on the step ‘of departure’, here step 1 of the analysis tree ‘Modeling’, and four other steps.

Call function ‘steps’
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$workflow$steps))

this (env)

The this binding is again a self-reference of the environment. It facilitates function calls to make a reference to the environment itself.

Call ‘this’ element
listviewer::jsonedit(as.list(envATModelingStep1$workflow$this))

changedAndOutdatedFiles

The function changedAndOutdatedFiles() identifies those files within a workflow which were changed or are outdated, and hence require a re-execution of the relevant step(s).

As changed are those files considered whose content has been modified after the relevant step with in the workflow had been last been executed.

In this context ‘changed’ means that a file has been modified after the relevant step had been executed for the last time. ‘Outdated’ refers to those files which have a broken dependency link, as indicated by the outdatedLink==TRUE in their metadata.

changedAndOutdatedFiles() has an optional tree parameter which restricts the check for changed and outdated files to a specific analysis tree within the workflow.

Call changeAndOutdatedFiles()
envATModelingStep1$workflow$changedAndOutdatedFiles()

rerunChangedAndOutdated

The ‘rerunChangedAndOutdated()’ function performs incremental workflow execution by only re-running steps that have changed or outdated dependencies, plus optionally their downstream consumers.

Internally, it

  1. Creates a selective execution plan by calling createReexecutionPlan()
  2. Identifies steps which need to be re-executed
  3. Executes the plan
  4. Returns the result invisibly

Comparison to other functions:

  • rerunAll(): Rebuilds everything from scratch
  • rerunChangedAndOutdated(): Only rebuilds what’s necessary
  • createReexecutionPlan(): Creates the plan but doesn’t execute it
Call rerunChangedAndOutdated
envATModelingStep1$workflow$rerunChangedAndOutdated()

createReexecutionPlan

The function creates a detailed execution plan for workflow steps that need to be re-executed, with proper dependency ordering and link management.

Call createReexecutionPlan
envATModelingStep1$workflow$createReexecutionPlan()

createTemplate

createTemplate() allows to create a reusable template from an existing workflow. This template can then be instantiated in a different environment.

Internally, calling createTemplate() calls ‘createWorkflowTemplateEnv()’ which extracts the workflow structure including remote files, preserves relatiosnhips, and builds template methods. Most critically, it applies ‘createSteptEmplateEnv()’ to each of the workflow’s step.

The resulting template environment provides:

Workflow-level methods:

  • df(): List all steps as data frame
  • setWorkflowTreeIdent(treeIdent): Set target tree
  • createExecutionPlan(): Generate execution order
  • executePlan(plan): Execute steps in order
  • realise(): Execute entire workflow

Step-level methods (per step template):

  • File management: addStepLocalFile(), addStepRemoteFile()
  • Relationships: lineage, usage, parent, children environments
  • Configuration: setStepValue(), addStepGridArgument()
  • Execution: realise() – Create actual step instance
Function ’createTemplate
envATModelingStep1$workflow$createTemplate()

df

The ‘df()’ function provides a tabular view of all steps in the workflow, combining their metadata into a single data frame for analysis and inspection.

The returned data frame contains:

  • fullName: Step identifier/name
  • description: Step description
  • rationale: Why this step exists
  • sourceEntityId: Server resource ID
  • sourceName: Original step name
  • treeIdent: Workflow tree identifier
  • handle: Unique step handle
  • processes: Process configurations
  • remoteFiles: Input file references
  • localFiles: Local file references
  • extLinks: External links
Call function df()
envATModelingStep1$workflow$df()

3 createStep

3.1 Purpose of the function

The createStep function creates new steps within improveR workflow trees. These steps serve as the foundational building blocks for structured data analysis workflows.

This function is essential for expanding existing workflows with new analytical components. It enables users to add steps that can execute specific tools, processes, or analytical procedures within a defined workflow context.

Key capabilities include:

  • Creating steps with specific tool configurations
  • Establishing parent-child relationships between steps
  • Defining process definitions that integrate with the workflow execution framework
  • Supporting both independent step creation and hierarchical step creation

The function facilitates the construction of complex multi-step analytical pipelines by automatically attaching new steps to parent steps when specified.

3.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, createStep serves as the foundational constructor that works in conjunction with attachStep and detachStep for building and reorganizing workflow hierarchies . It integrates closely with getStep by creating step entities that can subsequently be retrieved and manipulated through the step environment. The function connects with process management functions like createProcess and setProcessVariables by establishing the step framework that houses these computational definitions. In the broader improveR ecosystem, it interfaces with the resource management system through authenticated REST API calls to persist new steps on the server, connects with tool management systems to assign execution capabilities, and integrates with the workflow execution engine to enable the created steps to participate in automated workflow runs and dependency tracking.

3.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a validation-creation-registration pattern: first using loadResource to validate that the target tree exists and is accessible, then checking permissions through isAllowedTarget to ensure step creation is permitted within the specified context. The core operation constructs a step definition object with metadata including nodeType, tool configuration, runserver assignment, and optional parent step relationships. The function makes an authenticated POST request to /resources/{treeId}/steps endpoint with the step definition as the request payload to create the step on the server. After successful creation, it performs cache maintenance by calling unloadChildResources and unloadFullChildResources #REVIEW to ensure that subsequent navigation operations reflect the updated tree structure, finally returning the newly created step through loadResource to provide immediate access to the step entity.

3.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Create new step in demo tree
demoAnalysisTree <- loadResource(ident="/improve-tutorial/demoSteps")
demoAnalysisTreeIdent <- demoAnalysisTree$entityId
demoAnalysisTreeIdent

# Create a new independent step
## Note that the step name is assigned automatically
newStep <- createStep(treeIdent = demoAnalysisTreeIdent)

# Verify creation
newStep[, c("name", "path", "entityId")]
newStep$entityId

# Create another step which is now attached to the previously created step
parentStepIdent <- newStep$entityId
parentStepIdent

newChildStep <- createStep(
    treeIdent = demoAnalysisTreeIdent,
    parentStepIdent = parentStepIdent
)

# Verify creation
newChildStep[, c("name", "path", "entityId")]
newStep[,c("name", "path", "entityId")]

# Verify parent-child relationship
children <- loadChildSteps(parentStepIdent)$data[[1]]
children[, c("name", "path", "entityId")]

Note that when calling loadChildStep, the detatils on the child step(s) are stored in the list column data and not on the the dataframe’s top level.

4 attachStep

4.1 Purpose of the function

The attachStep function establishes hierarchical relationships between steps in improveR workflows by attaching a step to another step that serves as its parent. This function is essential for creating structured hierarchies that reflect the logical flow and dependencies between analytical steps. It provides flexibility to reorganize existing workflows, insert new steps into established processes, or correct relationships that were initially configured incorrectly, while maintaining workflow integrity and enabling proper execution planning and dependency 1tracking.

4.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, attachStep forms a complementary pair with detachStep for managing step hierarchy, working together with createStep to provide complete workflow structure control. The function integrates closely with navigation functions like getStep, loadParentStep, and loadChildSteps by ensuring cached relationships are updated through unloadParentStep calls. In the broader improveR ecosystem, it connects with the resource management system via loadResource for validation and uses the authentication infrastructure to make REST API calls that persist hierarchical changes across the entire system.

4.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a validation-execution pattern: first using loadResource to validate both step and parent entities exist, then extracting the tree identifier to determine the workflow context. The core operation makes an authenticated PUT request to /resources/{treeId}/steps/{stepId}/attachStepToParent with query parameters specifying the parent step ID. After the successful API call, the function calls unloadParentStep to invalidate cached parent-step relationships, ensuring subsequent navigation operations reflect the new hierarchy rather than stale cached data.

4.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Attach Step 2 to Step 1
step1Parent <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 1"
step2Child <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 2"

attachStep(ident=step2Child, parent=step1Parent)

5 detachStep

5.1 Purpose of the function

The detachStep function removes the hierarchical relationship between a step and its parent. This function is essential for workflow reorganization, allowing users to isolate steps that were incorrectly attached, flatten complex hierarchies, or prepare steps for reassignment to different parents. It provides the flexibility to modify workflow structures without deleting steps or losing their content, while maintaining data integrity and ensuring that cached relationships are properly updated throughout the system.

5.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, detachStep works as the complementary counterpart to attachStep, providing the opposite operation for managing step hierarchies. It integrates with navigation functions like loadParentStep and loadChildSteps by updating cached parent-child relationships through unloadChildSteps and unloadParentStep calls. The function works seamlessly with createStep and other step management functions to provide complete control of the analysis’ structure. In the broader improveR ecosystem, it connects with the resource management system via loadResource for step validation and uses the authentication infrastructure to make REST API calls that persist structural changes across the distributed system.

5.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a validation-execution-cleanup pattern: first using loadResource to validate the step entity exists and retrieve its metadata, then extracting the tree identifier and loading the parent step information. The core operation makes an authenticated PUT request to /resources/{treeId}/steps/{stepId}/detachStepFromParent with the step ID and tree ID as URL parameters. After the successful API call, the function performs cache maintenance by calling unloadChildSteps on the parent step and unloadParentStep on the detached step, ensuring that subsequent navigation operations reflect the updated hierarchy rather than stale cached relationships.

5.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Detach step from parent step
step2Child <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 2"

detachStep(ident=step2Child)

6 changeStepDescription

6.1 Purpose of the function

The changeStepDescription function modifies the description field of an existing step, allowing users to update documentation and clarify the purpose of analytical steps after they have been created. This function is instrumental for maintaining clear and accurate documentation as analyses evolve, requirements change, or when steps need better descriptions for collaboration and reproducibility. It enables dynamic updating of step metadata without requiring recreation of the entire step or disruption of existing workflow structures and dependencies.

6.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, changeStepDescription works alongside changeStepRationale to provide comprehensive metadata editing capabilities for workflow steps. Both functions share similar implementation patterns and complement getStep for retrieving step information before modification. The function integrates with improveR’s resource management system through loadResource and updateResource, ensuring that description changes are properly persisted and cached correctly. It connects to the broader improveR package’s authentication and REST API infrastructure, making authenticated calls to update step metadata on the server while maintaining data consistency across the distributed system.

6.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a load-modify-save pattern: first calling loadResource to retrieve the current step entity and validate it exists, then directly modifying the description property of the step entity object. The function makes an authenticated PUT request to the /resources/{resourceId}/ endpoint, sending the modified step entity as the request payload to persist changes on the server. Finally, it calls updateResource to refresh the local cache with the updated step information, ensuring that subsequent operations work with the most current data and maintaining consistency between local and server state.

6.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Change description of Step 1
stepIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 1"

loadResource(stepIdent)$description
## [1] "changed description"

changeStepDescription(ident=stepIdent, description="changed description")

7 changeStepRationale

7.1 Purpose of the function

The changeStepRationale function modifies the rationale field of an existing step, allowing users to update the reasoning and justification for why analytical steps were created and included in the workflow. This function is essential for maintaining clear analytical documentation that explains the scientific or methodological rationale behind each step, supporting reproducible research practices and regulatory compliance. It enables dynamic updating of step justification without requiring recreation of the entire step or disruption of existing workflow structures and dependencies, ensuring that analytical decisions remain well-documented as projects evolve.

7.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, changeStepRationale works as a companion to changeStepDescription to provide comprehensive metadata editing capabilities for steps. Both functions share identical implementation patterns and complement getStep for retrieving step information before modification. The function integrates seamlessly with improveR’s resource management system through loadResource and updateResource, ensuring that rationale changes are properly persisted and cached correctly. It connects to the broader improveR package’s authentication and REST API infrastructure, making authenticated calls to update step metadata on the server while maintaining data consistency and version control across the distributed system.

7.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows the same load-modify-save pattern as changeStepDescription: first calling loadResource to retrieve the current step entity and validate it exists, then directly modifying the rationale property of the step entity object. The function makes an authenticated PUT request to the /resources/{resourceId}/ endpoint, sending the modified step as the request payload to persist changes on the server. Finally, it calls updateResource to refresh the local cache with the updated step information, ensuring that subsequent operations work with the most current data and maintaining consistency between local and server state.

8 createStepEnv

8.1 Purpose of the function

The createStepEnv function constructs a specialized R environment object that encapsulates a step’s complete context and provides programmatic access to all step-related data and operations. This environment serves as a comprehensive interface containing the step’s metadata, file relationships, navigation capabilities, and workflow context in a structured, object-like format. The function creates an environment that includes nested sub-environments for children, parent, usage, and lineage relationships, along with functional bindings for operations like getStepInventory(), getStepResource(), and getStepState(). This environment-based approach enables intuitive navigation through workflow hierarchies using R’s $ operator and provides a unified API for step manipulation and introspection that supports both interactive analysis and programmatic workflow management.

8.2 Relation to other functions

Within the step functions family, createStepEnv serves as the foundational building block that underlies getStep(), which calls createStepEnv internally to generate the rich environment objects that users interact with. The function works closely with navigation functions like loadChildSteps, loadParentStep, and workflow analysis functions by providing the structured environment that contains lazy-loading mechanisms for these relationships. It integrates with resource management functions through embedded loadResource calls and connects with the broader improveR ecosystem by creating environments that interface with authentication systems, caching mechanisms, and REST API endpoints. The environments created by createStepEnv also support workflow execution functions by providing access to process definitions, file dependencies, and execution state information necessary for step orchestration and dependency tracking.

8.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a multi-layered environment construction pattern: first calling loadResource to retrieve the step’s core metadata and validate existence, then systematically building nested environments for relationships (children, parent, usage, lineage) with lazy-loading load() functions. The function creates functional bindings by embedding closures that capture the step context, enabling methods like getStepInventory() and getStepWithoutCache() to operate within the step’s scope. It constructs a workflow environment that provides access to execution planning and dependency analysis capabilities when populated. The function also creates a self-referential this binding and embeds the step’s dataframe representation (stepDf) with process and file metadata, resulting in a comprehensive environment that serves as both a data container and an operational interface for step management within the improveR workflow system.

8.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Create step environment using getStepDf and explore its structure
stepIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 1"

# First, get the stepDf (step metadata) using the internal function
# Note: Users typically use getStep() instead of calling createStepEnv directly
stepDf <- improveR:::getStepDf(stepIdent)
workflow <- createWorkflow()

# Create the step environment with the stepDf
step_env <- createStepEnv(stepDf, workflow)

# Examine the environment structure
class(step_env)
length(ls(step_env))
ls(step_env)

# Show the stepDf structure that was used to create the environment
names(stepDf)
stepDf$sourceName
stepDf$description

# Test functional bindings
step_env$getStepState()
step_resource <- step_env$getStepResource()
names(step_resource)[1:5]  # Show first few column names

# Explore nested environment structure  
ls(step_env$children)
ls(step_env$parent)
ls(step_env$workflow)

# Compare with getStep() which internally calls createStepEnv
step_env_via_getStep <- getStep(stepIdent)
identical(class(step_env), class(step_env_via_getStep))

9 getWorkflow

9.1 Purpose of the function

getWorkflow creates a workflow environment by transforming hierarchical collection of steps into a cohesive workflow object with built-in execution capabilities, dependency tracking, and orchestration methods. It enables users to work with entire workflows as single entities rather than managing individual steps separately, supporting complex analytical pipelines that require coordinated execution, dependency management, and workflow-level operations like template creation, execution planning, and incremental re-execution based on changes.

9.2 How it relates to other functions and the wider improveR package

getWorkflow serves as a higher-level aggregation function that internally calls getStep for each step in the target tree, building upon the individual step environments to create workflow-level functionality. It integrates closely with workflow execution functions like createWorkflow, providing the foundation for workflow templates and execution planning. The function connects with resource navigation functions through loadChildResources to discover all steps within a tree and works alongside workflow orchestration functions by creating environments that support methods like rerunAll(), createTemplate(), and executePlan(). In the broader improveR ecosystem, it bridges individual step management with workflow-level operations, enabling users to transition seamlessly between step-focused and workflow-focused analytical approaches while maintaining full access to both individual step capabilities and coordinated workflow execution.

9.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a discovery-and-aggregation pattern: first calling loadChildResources to retrieve all child resources from the specified tree identifier, then filtering the results to include only resources with nodeType=="Step" to exclude folders and other non-step entities. The function optionally excludes the current step (when includeSelf=FALSE) by comparing resource IDs with the current working directory step. It creates a temporary environment (tmpEnv) to accumulate workflow state and iterates through each discovered step using byNotEmpty, calling getStep for each step while progressively building the shared workflow environment. Each step environment created by getStep receives and contributes to the evolving workflow context through the workflow parameter, enabling cross-step dependency tracking and workflow-level method binding. If no steps are found, the function creates an empty workflow using createWorkflow(), ensuring a valid workflow environment is always returned for subsequent operations.

9.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Create workflow from analysis tree
# Get workflow from an analysis tree
stepIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 10"
envWorkflow <- getWorkflow(ident=stepIdent)

# treeIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/DataOrder"
# envWorkflow <- getWorkflow(ident=treeIdent) 

treeIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/Modeling"
envWorkflow <- getWorkflow(ident=treeIdent) #joins working  

# Examine the workflow structure
class(envWorkflow)
ls(envWorkflow)
listviewer::jsonedit(list(envWorkflow))

# Access workflow-level operations
envWorkflow$df()  # View all steps as dataframe
envWorkflow$steps  # Access individual step environments

# Workflow execution capabilities
# workflow$rerunAll()  # Re-execute entire workflow
# workflow$rerunChangedAndOutdated()  # Incremental execution

# Create workflow template for reuse
template <- workflow$createTemplate()

# Example with includeSelf parameter
currentStepIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/Modeling/Step 1"
workflowWithSelf <- getWorkflow(currentStepIdent, includeSelf = TRUE)
workflowWithoutSelf <- getWorkflow(currentStepIdent, includeSelf = FALSE)

# Compare step counts
length(ls(workflowWithSelf$steps))
length(ls(workflowWithoutSelf$steps))

10 finishRunResource

10.1 Purpose of the function

The finishRunResource function provides a blocking mechanism that waits for a step to complete execution, serving as an essential synchronization tool in improveR. This function monitors the execution status of a running step and blocks further code execution until the step reaches a “FINISHED” state, enabling sequential workflow orchestration where subsequent steps depend on the completion of previous ones. It offers optional validation to ensure steps complete using specific runserver and tool configurations, providing quality control for reproducible analyses. The function is crucial for automated pipeline execution, batch processing scenarios, and any situation where precise control over step execution timing is required to maintain workflow integrity and data dependencies.

10.2 Relation to other functions

finishRunResource forms a complementary pair with runStepResource, providing the “wait for completion” counterpart to step execution initiation. It integrates closely with workflow orchestration functions by enabling proper sequencing of dependent steps and connects with step state management through continuous polling of step status. The function works alongside resource management functions like updateResource to maintain current step information and integrates with the broader improveR ecosystem through authentication systems for server communication. It supports workflow execution engines by providing the synchronization primitives necessary for complex multi-step analytical pipelines, and connects with process management functions to validate tool and runserver configurations during execution completion.

10.3 Under the hood

The implementation follows a polling-based monitoring pattern with optional tool validation: first calling updateResource to retrieve current step status and validate the step exists, then entering a continuous polling loop that checks the step’s runStatus every 5 seconds using Sys.sleep(5). When runserver and tool parameters are provided, the function performs additional validation by calling getToolId to resolve expected tool identifiers and actualLoadProcessesForStep to retrieve process information for comparison. The core monitoring logic uses actualLoadProcessRuns to identify the most recent execution run and compares tool identifiers to ensure the step completed with the correct configuration. The function maintains state through variables like running, wrongRun, and toolId to track execution progress and prevent false positives from previous runs with different tool configurations. The polling continues until either the step reaches “FINISHED” status (when no tool validation is required) or until it reaches “FINISHED” status with the correct tool configuration, finally returning the step identifier invisibly.

10.4 Example for demonstration purposes

Wait for step execution to complete
# Start a step execution
stepIdent <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 1"
runStepResource(stepIdent)

# Wait for the step to complete (basic usage)
finishRunResource(stepIdent)

# Wait for step to complete with specific tool validation
finishRunResource(
  ident = stepIdent,
  runserverName = "runserver",
  runserverToolName = "R_4.2"
)

# Example of sequential step execution
step1 <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 1"
step2 <- "/improve-tutorial/demoSteps/Step 2"

# Run and wait for first step
runStepResource(step1)
finishRunResource(step1)

# Now safely run the second step knowing first is complete
runStepResource(step2)
finishRunResource(step2)

print("Both steps completed successfully")
